title: Regulating Act 1773
definition: The Regulating Act 1773 was the first landmark parliamentary intervention by the British Crown to control and regulate the administration of the East India Company (EIC) in India, transitioning it from a purely commercial body to a semi-sovereign administrative entity.
importanceInUpsc: This topic is foundational for both UPSC Prelims (GS-1 Modern History & Polity) and Mains (GS-2: Evolution of the Indian Constitution, Historical Underpinnings). Questions test the shift from decentralization to centralization, the establishment of the Supreme Court at Calcutta, and the structural flaws that necessitated subsequent acts like Pitt's India Act 1784.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of the Regulating Act 1773.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions of early British administration.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions regarding Governor-General powers and Council dynamics.
prerequisites: Battle of Plassey (1757) and Battle of Buxar (1764)
Grant of Diwani rights in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa (1765)
Dual Government system of Robert Clive
